title: Outcome Target
description: Reverse-forecast planning input: the buyer states the outcome needed and the seller plans against it. The goal uses the forecastable-metric vocabulary for delivery metrics and the event-type vocabulary for conversion events, so every permitted goal has a defined answer: forecast points carry the goal's metric or event key in metrics, with forecast_range_unit 'clicks' or 'conversions' structuring the curve where those units apply. Three request shapes, at least one of volume or cost_per required: volume only, where the seller solves for budget and answers with total_budget_guidance; cost_per with a buyer budget (offer_filters.budget_range or the brief), where the seller plans the volume it can deliver within that budget at or below (cap) or around (target) the amount; and cost_per plus volume, where the seller plans toward the volume at the cost. Answer: for cost_per, each proposal states the cost the seller can actually plan to in commercial_terms.bidding.cost_per, in the proposal currency and with the buyer's strength. The amount MAY exceed the ask, but the strength MUST NOT change: a cap of 3 the seller can only meet at 4.50 returns {amount: 4.50, strength: 'cap'}, never 'target', and a seller that will not plan at any amount under the buyer's strength rejects instead. That policy binds by BiddingPolicy rules to the scope-bound primary optimization goal, which MUST match goal; forecast points carry the goal volume planned at that cost. Currency: cost_per carries a currency because BiddingPolicy.cost_per inherits the media-buy currency and none exists at request time. cost_per.currency MUST equal offer_filters.budget_range.currency when present, and commercial_terms.total_budget.currency, total_budget_guidance.currency, and forecast.currency on every answering proposal MUST equal it; sellers MUST NOT convert currency. Rejection: sellers not declaring media_buy.outcome_target MUST reject the field with UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE rather than silently ignore it. Declaring sellers MAY reject a goal they cannot plan against (for example 'spend', which restates budget) with INVALID_REQUEST naming criteria.outcome_target.goal, and MUST reject a cost_per they cannot plan against, including one in a currency the requested products are not priced in, with INVALID_REQUEST naming criteria.outcome_target.cost_per. Priorities, event sources, and vendor bindings stay on purchase optimization goals, which share this vocabulary. A planning input, not a delivery guarantee: obligations arise only at proposal finalization, and the accepted proposal's bidding.cost_per is the execution policy.

goal.description: The outcome to plan against: a seller-tracked delivery metric or an advertiser conversion event.

oneOf.description: Plan against a seller-tracked delivery metric. The response forecast carries this metric as a key in points' metrics.

metric.description: Delivery metric to plan for, in the same vocabulary forecast points report.

oneOf.description: Plan against an advertiser conversion event. The response forecast carries this event type as a key in points' metrics.

event_type.description: Conversion event to plan for, in the same vocabulary forecast points report.

custom_event_name.description: Required when event_type is 'custom'. Platform-specific name for the custom event.

volume.description: Desired total volume of the goal's metric or event across the planned flight. Optional when cost_per is present.

cost_per.description: Average cost the buyer will pay per goal result: BiddingPolicy.cost_per plus a currency. The seller answers in commercial_terms.bidding.cost_per with the same strength and the amount it can actually plan to, which MAY be higher than this amount.

amount.description: Average cost amount per goal result, denominated in currency.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of amount. BiddingPolicy.cost_per has no currency because it inherits the media-buy currency; no media-buy currency exists at request time, so the request states it here. It becomes the currency of every answering proposal and MUST equal offer_filters.budget_range.currency when a budget range is present.

strength.description: `cap` optimizes for an average at or below the amount and accepts underdelivery when necessary; `target` optimizes around the amount while balancing volume and spend. Neither is a per-result or per-auction guarantee. The seller's answer keeps this strength.
